baskingshark: A colossal gentle plankton-straining sea creature SWIMMING HEAD-ON STRAIGHT TOWARD THE VIEWER, seen FROM DIRECTLY IN FRONT so that we are looking straight into its open mouth down the length of its body. FROM THIS ANGLE THE ANIMAL IS ESSENTIALLY ONE ENORMOUS OPEN CIRCLE filling most of the picture: its jaws are stretched to their fullest and form a VAST PERFECTLY ROUND HOLLOW OPENING, a dark cavernous tunnel mouth like looking into the end of a barrel, a drainpipe or a cave mouth, wider than its own body. THE RIM OF THIS CIRCLE IS SMOOTH, BARE, PLAIN AND UNBROKEN ALL THE WAY AROUND, a clean soft even lip of grey skin like the rolled rim of a bucket, with a soft pale fringe of fine flexible hair-like combs visible deep inside the dark tunnel well behind that rim. Its small dark eyes sit far out on either side of the circle, and its short blunt snout rises just above the top of it. Behind the opening the grey-brown body tapers away from us, with the tips of its pectoral fins spread wide to either side and a tall triangular fin above. Slow, harmless, gentle and vast
sunfishmola: A giant ocean sunfish SEEN IN STRICT SIDE PROFILE, side-on to the viewer, showing its whole flank flat to us with ONE eye on the side of its head and its small round mouth at the front on the left. ITS BODY IS TALLER THAN IT IS LONG: the distance from the top of its back down to its belly is GREATER than the distance from its mouth back to its rear end, so the flank forms a HUGE ROUND UPRIGHT PLATE - a full moon, a dinner plate stood on edge, a car wheel - deep and round and squat, definitely NOT a long streamlined swimming shape and NOT oval and NOT elongated. Picture a circle with a face at one edge. It is squashed flat from side to side like a coin. THE REAR OF THE DISC IS SHEARED CLEAN AWAY, as though the back half had been sliced off with a knife straight down: the body ENDS abruptly in a blunt vertical cut edge trimmed with a short WAVY SCALLOPED FRILL of skin lying flush against it like a pie crust. NOTHING PROJECTS BEHIND OR BELOW - no tail, no fan, no fork. From the TOP of the circle ONE ENORMOUS POINTED FIN rises straight UP and from the BOTTOM one identical fin points straight DOWN. A tiny round mouth, one large round eye, small pectoral fins, rough mottled silver-grey hide
blackrhino_c: A very young rhinoceros calf seen from a THREE-QUARTER FRONT ANGLE, only a few months old, with infant proportions: an OVERSIZED HEAD too big for its body, SHORT STUBBY LEGS, a small rounded body, a soft rounded forehead and big soft eyes. THE LINE OF ITS FACE IS ONE SINGLE UNBROKEN SMOOTH CURVE running from between its ears, down over its forehead and along the whole length of its snout to its lip, like the smooth curve of an egg or the back of a spoon, with NOTHING TALL OR POINTED RISING ANYWHERE ALONG THAT LINE AT ANY POINT - no spike, no cone, no blade, no projection, no second growth of any kind, the profile stays smooth and rounded the whole way down. The only interruption anywhere on that curve is ONE SINGLE SMALL SOFT ROUNDED GREY PEBBLE-BUMP the size of its own eye, low and blunt and smooth, sitting flat on the snout like a river stone resting on a table - one bump only and nothing else. At the end of the curve, a POINTED HOOKED PREHENSILE UPPER LIP for browsing. Soft mid-grey skin, evenly lit, small tubular ears, a stubby tail
